seoTitle: Honningsvåg cruise port guide: North Cape by bus
seoDescription: Honningsvåg cruise quays are 2 min from the main street. North Cape is 33 km away: Line 406 bus, 3 hours with 75 min at the Cape and Hall entry included.
quickAnswer: Ships berth at quays beside the harbour building, a two-minute walk from the main street; on busy days one ship may anchor and tender to the inner harbour. The North Cape is 33 km away and cannot be reached on foot: the Line 406 North Cape Express bus from Tourist Information takes 3 hours return with 1 hour 15 minutes at the Cape, and its ticket includes North Cape Hall. Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard, or at the tender pontoon 90 minutes before.
intro: Honningsvåg is a small fishing town on Magerøya, and almost everyone who comes ashore here is heading for the North Cape plateau, 307 m above the Barents Sea. The town itself is compact: the quays, Tourist Information, the North Cape Museum and the main street sit within a few minutes of each other. The day is shaped by the 33 km road to the Cape, the weather on the exposed plateau, which can close the road, and the number of ships in port, which decides how quickly tour buses fill.
tenderNotes: Ships normally berth. The port has two tender piers and mooring buoys for tender operations, and on days with several large ships one may anchor and tender passengers to floating piers in the inner harbour, about a 10-minute ride.

terminals.name: Berth North (Port of North Cape)
terminals.notes: Main cruise berth, for ships up to 360 m. Next to the harbour building; Tourist Information and the North Cape Museum are a short walk away. Buses pick up near the terminal.

terminals.name: Berth 3
terminals.notes: Second cruise berth, for ships up to 260 m, in the same harbour area.

terminals.name: Inner-harbour tender pontoons
terminals.notes: Used only when a ship anchors on a busy day.

walkability.detail: The town centre starts at the quay. The main street, Tourist Information and museum are a few minutes' walk; Honningsvåg Church is about 800 m away, uphill. The North Cape is 33 km away and is not walkable.

transportSections.detail: Walk off the quay past the harbour building to Tourist Information, then along the main street.

transportSections.cost: Price not confirmed for 2026; the ticket includes North Cape Hall entry and the panoramic film
transportSections.time: 3 hours return, with 1 hour 15 minutes at the North Cape
transportSections.detail: Departs daily from Tourist Information in the centre; tickets are sold there and can be booked in advance. One departure is at 11:15, timed for Hurtigruten. On multi-ship days independent seats can sell out early, so book or buy as soon as you land.

transportSections.cost: Agree the fare before you go
transportSections.time: About 40 minutes each way in summer
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait in the car park in front of the dock, mainly in the morning. Fewer are around later, so arrange the return pick-up time with the driver.

transportSections.time: 45–75 minutes each way depending on conditions
transportSections.detail: Hire companies operate in the cruise terminal area. In winter the last stretch from Skarsvåg junction to the plateau is driven only in convoy behind a snowplough, at fixed times, and can close completely in bad weather.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard (16:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard). If your ship is tendering, be at the inner-harbour pontoon 90 minutes before. If you go to the North Cape independently, leave the plateau at least 165 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: The plateau road is exposed and can close or slow in wind, fog or snow. In winter the last 13 km run only in convoy at fixed times, so a missed convoy can mean hours of waiting. The 11:15 Line 406 bus returns about 14:15, leaving a comfortable margin.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If the road closes or you are delayed on the plateau, tell the North Cape Hall staff and phone the port agent number on your daily programme at once. Port harbour watch: +47 917 33 143.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Line 406 bus from Tourist Information, Hall entry included (2026 price not confirmed)

excursionAdvice: The ship's North Cape coach is the safe choice here, and for many passengers the sensible one: the ship waits for its own tours if the plateau road is delayed, and on a busy day the independent bus can be full. Go independently on the Line 406 bus only if you can get a ticket early and the timings leave a wide margin. In winter, when the road runs in convoy and closes in storms, book the ship's tour. The town itself needs no tour.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00, all-aboard is 17:30 and a summer day.

steps.what: Walk ashore to Tourist Information and buy or collect a ticket for the 11:15 Line 406 North Cape bus.
Walk the main street and the harbour; see the Bamse statue near Tourist Information.
Walk uphill to Honningsvåg Church, about 800 m, then back down.
Coffee and something warm in town. Put on windproof layers for the plateau.
Line 406 bus from Tourist Information to the North Cape.
75 minutes at the Cape: the globe monument, the cliff edge viewpoint, then North Cape Hall's film, exhibitions and Cave of Lights.
Back in Honningsvåg. Visit the North Cape Museum at Holmen 1 (open 11:00–16:00 in summer).
Last stop: king crab or fish soup near the harbour, or Ocean Stories.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: North Cape (Nordkapp) plateau
sights.why: The cliff top 307 m above the sea at the end of the E69, with the globe monument and views north over the Barents Sea.
sights.cost: Included in the Line 406 bus ticket (2026)
sights.tip: The plateau is often colder and windier than town and can be in fog. Take a windproof layer, hat and gloves even in July.

sights.name: North Cape Hall
sights.why: The visitor centre on the plateau: panoramic film, historical exhibitions and the Cave of Lights, plus a café, gift shop and, in summer, a restaurant, post office and Panorama Bar.
sights.cost: Ticket valid 24 hours and personal; under-5s free; included in the Line 406 bus ticket (2026)
sights.tip: Bring ID. The question of fees for access to the plateau itself was under appeal in 2026, so check what is charged on the day.

sights.name: North Cape Museum (Nordkappmuseet)
sights.why: Two floors on Magerøya's 9,000-year settlement history, the 1944 burning of Honningsvåg and its rebuilding, North Cape tourism and coastal fishing life.
sights.tip: At Holmen 1 by the harbour, in the same building as Tourist Information. Summer hours 11:00–16:00 daily; shorter weekday hours the rest of the year.

sights.name: Honningsvåg Church
sights.why: The wooden church that was the only building left standing after the town was burned in 1944.
sights.tip: About 800 m from the port, uphill. Check for services before going in.

sights.name: Storfjellet stone staircase
sights.why: Sherpa-built stone steps above the town with views over the harbour and the Arctic sea.
sights.timeNeeded: Allow about 3 hours as a guided hike
sights.cost: Free on your own; guided tours are sold locally
sights.tip: Exposed in wind and wet; only for fit walkers with good shoes and a firm turn-back time.

sights.name: Ocean Stories
sights.why: Visitor centre run by Grieg Seafood in North Cape Harbour, opened in August 2025.
sights.tip: A good indoor option if the plateau is in fog.

sights.name: Bamse statue
sights.why: Statue honouring Bamse, a famous Saint Bernard dog.
sights.tip: Near Tourist Information; an easy photo stop on the way to the bus.

sights.name: Gjesværstappan bird reserve
sights.why: Nature reserve near Gjesvær on Magerøya, known for puffins and sea eagles; visited on local guided tours.
sights.cost: Tour prices vary; book with a local operator
sights.tip: Seasonal, roughly May to September. Combine it with the Cape only on a long call.

food.where: King crab dining experience on the 1952 fishermen's pier (seasonal, 21 May to early September)
Nor Café Bistro, Honningsvåg (open all year)
Sjøgata Pub at Perleporten Kulturhus, which brews its own beer
Julehuset (the Christmas House), Skarsvåg, on the road to the Cape

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning to walk to the North Cape.
commonMistakes.fix: It is 33 km away by road. Use the Line 406 bus, a taxi, a hire car or a ship's tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Waiting until late morning to buy a bus ticket on a multi-ship day.
commonMistakes.fix: Go straight to Tourist Information when you land, or book in advance.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dressing for the weather in town.
commonMistakes.fix: The plateau is more exposed and usually colder and windier. Take a windproof jacket, hat and gloves.

commonMistakes.mistake: Driving to the Cape in winter without checking the convoy times.
commonMistakes.fix: From Skarsvåg junction the road runs only in convoy at fixed times. Check Statens vegvesen's traffic service before setting off, and allow for closures.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming a taxi will be waiting for the return.
commonMistakes.fix: Taxis gather in the morning. Agree the return time with your driver before you leave town.

safety: Honningsvåg is a small, safe town. The real hazards are the weather and the road: wind, fog and snow on the exposed plateau, and winter closures of the last stretch to the Cape. Keep well back from the cliff edge outside the fenced areas. On the Storfjellet steps and any hill walk, wet rock and sudden wind are the dangers; turn back early. Reindeer graze near the road in summer, so drivers should slow down.
scams: No scams specific to Honningsvåg were found in the sources checked. The main money risk is a non-refundable independent tour that cannot run when the plateau road closes, so check cancellation terms.
accessibility: The quays, Tourist Information, the museum and the main street are close together on fairly level ground near the harbour. The church is uphill. At the North Cape, North Cape Hall is the sheltered indoor option, while the plateau itself is open, windy ground. Ask the bus or tour operator in advance about step-free access to the vehicle. If your ship tenders, boarding depends on the swell; ask the ship whether wheelchair users can transfer.
rainyDay: Fog or rain often hides the view from the plateau, but North Cape Hall's film, exhibitions and Cave of Lights are indoors. In town, the North Cape Museum, Ocean Stories and the cafés along the harbour fill a wet afternoon. Skip the Storfjellet steps in rain or strong wind.
crowdTips: Honningsvåg handled 173 cruise calls and about 200,000 passengers in 2024. On days with several large ships, buses and the plateau are busiest when the ships' tours arrive. Buy your bus ticket first thing, explore the town while the tour coaches are on the plateau, and visit the museum in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Is Honningsvåg walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. The quays are beside the harbour building and the main street is a two-minute walk. The North Cape is 33 km away and is not walkable.

faqs.q: How do I get from Honningsvåg cruise port to the North Cape?
faqs.a: Take the Line 406 North Cape Express bus from Tourist Information: 3 hours return with 1 hour 15 minutes at the Cape, North Cape Hall entry included. Taxis, hire cars and ship's tours are the alternatives.
Usually not. Ships berth at Berth North or Berth 3. On busy days a ship may anchor and tender passengers to floating piers in the inner harbour.

faqs.q: Is the North Cape road open in winter?
faqs.a: The last stretch from Skarsvåg junction is driven only in convoy behind a snowplough at fixed times, and it closes completely in severe weather.

faqs.q: What is included in the North Cape Hall ticket?
faqs.a: The panoramic film, the historical exhibitions and the Cave of Lights. It is valid for 24 hours, is personal, and children under 5 enter free.

faqs.q: What can I do in Honningsvåg in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The North Cape by bus, then the North Cape Museum, the church and the harbour in town. On a long summer call, add a bird-cliff boat trip from Gjesvær.
Yes. Prepare for cold wind on the plateau and keep away from unfenced cliff edges.
